body: The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency located between the UK and Ireland. For country streaks, it is considered part of the United Kingdom.
Coverage on the Isle of Man is exclusively Generation 2. This is identifiable by its lower camera quality, distinctive circular blur, and slightly off colors.
The Isle of Man uses white front and yellow rear licence plates, similar to the UK. A key distinction is the red strip on the left side of the plate.
The landscape of the Isle of Man is characterized by hilly farmland and narrow roads.
Similar to Ireland, houses with whitewashed walls and entrance walls are common on the Isle of Man.
Striped kerbs can sometimes be seen along main roads.
Blue bollards can commonly be found in urban areas.
Gorse plants with bright yellow flowers are very common on the Isle of Man, though they can also be found in other rugged areas of the UK and Ireland.
The Isle of Man is generally quite hilly, with a few exceptions.
The northern part of the Isle of Man is very flat, in contrast to the rest of the island. It's common to see mountains to the south from this area.
A ‘twig smudge’ on the left side of the camera lens is a unique meta for the southern Isle of Man.
Douglas, the capital, is recognizable by its higher population density and rows of terraced houses.
The town of Laxey is located in a northwest-southeast valley.
A generic lamp with a blue base and a small blue sticker is found on most of the island. The top two letters on the sticker can narrow down the location to one of the 21 parishes.
All-green lamps are commonly found in Ramsey and Castletown, and more rarely in the Malew, Santon, and Garff parishes.
Lamps in Douglas have a small white sticker with 2 green numbers.
In southern Onchan, lamps have a small yellow sticker where the two letters are the initials of the road name.
Many street signs in Ramsey feature the oval shaped coat of arms.
In Port Erin, many signs have the coat of arms placed above the text.
The Ronaldsway Airport can be recognized by the large, flat and open field with a boundary fence.
The Peel castle, which sits atop an island, can be seen in Peel.
